title: Level Crossings, Tunnels & Narrow Roads
whatItIs: A large, long or slow vehicle could still be on a level crossing when a train arrives. Obey every sign to phone the signal operator, keep your distance in tunnels and use passing places.

keyFacts.text: Large or slow vehicle: you MUST obey any sign telling you to use the railway telephone to get permission to cross.
You MUST also telephone again when you are clear of the crossing, if asked to.
You MUST obey safe height signs at overhead electric lines: clearance is usually 5 m but may be lower.

keyFacts: Never drive onto a crossing until the road beyond is clear. Never stop or park on or near one.
Large vehicle in a tunnel: allow a four-second gap. If you stop, leave at least 5 metres.
Single-track road: pull into a passing place on your left, or wait opposite one on your right.

visual.caption: Using the railway telephone at a level crossing

items.title: Park in the marked place
items.text: Some crossings mark a place for large or slow vehicles to park while phoning.

items.title: Phone the signal operator
items.text: Use the railway telephone and get permission to cross.

items.title: Cross only when clear
items.text: Only when the road is clear on the other side.

items.title: Phone again if asked
items.text: When clear of the crossing, phone again if asked to.

a.label: Steady amber light
points: Means stop, unless it is unsafe to do so
Already over the white line? Keep going

b.label: Flashing red lights
points: You MUST stop behind the white line
Still flashing after a train? Another train is coming

onTheTest.question: Your long, low lorry could ground on a level crossing. A sign tells you to phone before crossing. What must you do?
options: Phone the signal operator and get permission to cross
Cross slowly if no train is in sight
Sound your horn and cross quickly
Wait for another vehicle to cross first
onTheTest.why: Drivers of large, slow or long, low vehicles must obey any sign telling them to use the railway telephone to get permission to cross.

onTheTest.question: Your lorry breaks down on a level crossing. What should you do first?
options: Get everyone out of the vehicle and clear of the crossing
Keep trying to restart the engine
Phone your transport office for advice
Switch on hazard lights and wait in the cab
onTheTest.why: Get everyone out and clear of the crossing immediately, then use a railway telephone to tell the signal operator.

traps: Never zig-zag round half-barriers: they come down because a train is approaching.
If your lorry touches a height barrier or bells, don't continue onto the railway.
Red lights flashing for over 3 minutes with no train (not at full barriers)? Phone the signal operator.
Single-track road: give way to vehicles coming uphill whenever you can.
